hints: Identify the three mutually exclusive ways all three cars can have the same colour: all white (WWW), all black (BBB), or all silver (SSS).
Because selections are without replacement, reduce the numerator and denominator by 1 on each successive draw: P(WWW) = (8/16)(7/15)(6/14), P(BBB) = (5/16)(4/15)(3/14), P(SSS) = (3/16)(2/15)(1/14).
Add the three probabilities: 336/3360 + 60/3360 + 6/3360 = 402/3360, which simplifies to 67/560 = 0.120 (3 s.f.).
walkthrough:
Identify the three mutually exclusive outcomes where all three cars are the same colour:
$$\text{Event} = \text{all White } (WWW) \cup \text{all Black } (BBB) \cup \text{all Silver } (SSS)$$

Compute the probability of each outcome without replacement from 16 cars:
$$\mathrm{P}(WWW) = \frac{8}{16} \times \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{6}{14} = \frac{336}{3360} = \frac{1}{10}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(BBB) = \frac{5}{16} \times \frac{4}{15} \times \frac{3}{14} = \frac{60}{3360} = \frac{1}{56}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(SSS) = \frac{3}{16} \times \frac{2}{15} \times \frac{1}{14} = \frac{6}{3360} = \frac{1}{560}$$

Sum the three probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{same colour}) = \frac{336 + 60 + 6}{3360} = \frac{402}{3360} = \frac{67}{560} \approx 0.120\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the composition of the bag:
- Total number of cars: $8 + 5 + 3 = 16$
- White cars: $8$
- Black cars: $5$
- Silver cars: $3$
Three cars are chosen at random without replacement.

Step 2: List the three mutually exclusive ways all 3 cars can share the same colour:
- Case 1: All 3 cars are White ($WWW$)
- Case 2: All 3 cars are Black ($BBB$)
- Case 3: All 3 cars are Silver ($SSS$)

Step 3: Calculate the probability of each case using conditional probabilities:
- For Case 1 ($WWW$):
$$\mathrm{P}(WWW) = \frac{8}{16} \times \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{6}{14} = \frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{16 \times 15 \times 14} = \frac{336}{3360} = \frac{1}{10}$$
- For Case 2 ($BBB$):
$$\mathrm{P}(BBB) = \frac{5}{16} \times \frac{4}{15} \times \frac{3}{14} = \frac{5 \times 4 \times 3}{16 \times 15 \times 14} = \frac{60}{3360} = \frac{1}{56}$$
- For Case 3 ($SSS$):
$$\mathrm{P}(SSS) = \frac{3}{16} \times \frac{2}{15} \times \frac{1}{14} = \frac{3 \times 2 \times 1}{16 \times 15 \times 14} = \frac{6}{3360} = \frac{1}{560}$$

Step 4: Add the probabilities using a common denominator of $3360$:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{same colour}) = \frac{336}{3360} + \frac{60}{3360} + \frac{6}{3360} = \frac{336 + 60 + 6}{3360} = \frac{402}{3360}$$
Divide the numerator and denominator by 6:
$$\frac{402 \div 6}{3360 \div 6} = \frac{67}{560}$$
In decimal form:
$$\frac{67}{560} = 0.119642\dots \approx 0.120\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

hints: Break down the requirement of at least 1 white and at least 1 black into the three possible colour compositions for the 3 cars: (2 white, 1 black), (1 white, 2 black), and (1 white, 1 black, 1 silver).
For 2 white and 1 black, there are 3 orderings: 3 * (8/16) * (7/15) * (5/14) = 840/3360.
walkthrough:
Partition the event into three mutually exclusive scenarios containing at least 1 white and at least 1 black car:
$$\text{Scenarios: } (2W, 1B), \quad (1W, 2B), \quad (1W, 1B, 1S)$$

Calculate the probability for each scenario:
$$\mathrm{P}(2W, 1B) = 3 \times \left(\frac{8}{16} \times \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{5}{14}\right) = \frac{840}{3360}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(1W, 2B) = 3 \times \left(\frac{8}{16} \times \frac{5}{15} \times \frac{4}{14}\right) = \frac{480}{3360}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(1W, 1B, 1S) = 6 \times \left(\frac{8}{16} \times \frac{5}{15} \times \frac{3}{14}\right) = \frac{720}{3360}$$

Add the probabilities of the three scenarios:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{at least } 1W \text{ and at least } 1B) = \frac{840 + 480 + 720}{3360} = \frac{2040}{3360} = \frac{17}{28} \approx 0.607\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify all valid compositions satisfying the condition:
We must select 3 cars such that there is at least one White ($W$) and at least one Black ($B$). The available colours are White (8), Black (5), and Silver (3).
The possible compositions of $(W, B, S)$ summing to 3 are:
- Composition 1: 2 White, 1 Black, 0 Silver ($WWB$)
- Composition 2: 1 White, 2 Black, 0 Silver ($WBB$)
- Composition 3: 1 White, 1 Black, 1 Silver ($WBS$)

Step 2: Method 1 using draw probabilities:
- For Composition 1 ($WWB$):
There are $\frac{3!}{2!1!} = 3$ arrangements of the draws ($WWB, WBW, BWW$).
$$\mathrm{P}(WWB) = 3 \times \left(\frac{8}{16} \times \frac{7}{15} \times \frac{5}{14}\right) = 3 \times \frac{280}{3360} = \frac{840}{3360}$$
- For Composition 2 ($WBB$):
There are $\frac{3!}{1!2!} = 3$ arrangements ($WBB, BWB, BBW$).
$$\mathrm{P}(WBB) = 3 \times \left(\frac{8}{16} \times \frac{5}{15} \times \frac{4}{14}\right) = 3 \times \frac{160}{3360} = \frac{480}{3360}$$
- For Composition 3 ($WBS$):
There are $3! = 6$ arrangements of the three distinct colours.
$$\mathrm{P}(WBS) = 6 \times \left(\frac{8}{16} \times \frac{5}{15} \times \frac{3}{14}\right) = 6 \times \frac{120}{3360} = \frac{720}{3360}$$

Step 3: Sum the probabilities of all valid compositions:
$$\text{Total Probability} = \frac{840 + 480 + 720}{3360} = \frac{2040}{3360}$$
Divide numerator and denominator by 120:
$$\frac{2040 \div 120}{3360 \div 120} = \frac{17}{28}$$
In decimal form:
$$\frac{17}{28} = 0.607142\dots \approx 0.607\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

Step 4: Alternative check using combinations:
Total ways to choose 3 cars from 16:
$$\binom{16}{3} = \frac{16 \times 15 \times 14}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 560$$
Favourable combinations:
- $\binom{8}{2} \times \binom{5}{1} = 28 \times 5 = 140$
- $\binom{8}{1} \times \binom{5}{2} = 8 \times 10 = 80$
- $\binom{8}{1} \times \binom{5}{1} \times \binom{3}{1} = 8 \times 5 \times 3 = 120$
Total favourable $= 140 + 80 + 120 = 340$.
Probability $= \frac{340}{560} = \frac{17}{28} \approx 0.607$.
